references.text: The murder of Abel – the first innocent blood shed. Jesus refers to the blood of the prophets that has been shed "from the foundation of the world," and Abel's blood is the first example of this in Scripture ([ref:1 Mos 4:8-11|Genesis 4:8-11]).

The murder of Zechariah, son of the priest Jehoiada, in the temple courtyard. This is traditionally regarded as the last prophetic murder in the canonical order of the Hebrew Bible, and together with Abel's blood forms the framework Jesus points to ([ref:2 Krøn 24:20-22|2 Chronicles 24:20-22]).

Jeremiah testifies that the Lord sent prophets again and again to the people, but they would not listen. This underscores the recurring pattern that the blood of the prophets was shed because the people rejected them ([ref:Jer 26:15|Jeremiah 26:15]).

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says that all righteous blood shed on earth, from Abel's blood to Zechariah, son of Berechiah, will be required of this generation ([ref:Matt 23:35-36|Matthew 23:35-36]).

The immediate context in which Jesus accuses the Pharisees of building the tombs of the prophets while being children of those who killed them, and where God's wisdom says that prophets and apostles will be sent and killed ([ref:Luk 11:47-49|Luke 11:47-49]).
The following verse that specifies Jesus' words by mentioning Abel and Zechariah as the extremes of the innocent blood that must be avenged ([ref:Luk 11:51|Luke 11:51]).

In Revelation it is said about Babylon that "in her was found the blood of prophets and saints, and of all who have been slain on earth" – the eschatological reckoning with the persecution of the prophets that Jesus warns of here ([ref:Åp 18:24|Revelation 18:24]).

Paul writes that the Jews "killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and persecuted us," and that they fill up their sins to the full – an echo of Jesus' words that this generation's measure of sin will be completed ([ref:1 Tess 2:15-16|1 Thessalonians 2:15-16]).
